resumen: Lying face down on an inclined bench, you row two dumbbells towards the hips with the elbows going back. The supported chest takes the load off the lower back.
ejecucion: Set the back rest to about 30-45° and lie face down with your chest supported at the top and your feet on the floor, with a dumbbell on the floor at each side of the bench, so you can pick them up once lying down.
Let a dumbbell hang in each hand with straight arms and palms facing each other.
Row the dumbbells by driving your elbows back, close to your body, until they are level with your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the end and lower under control until your arms are straight.
Keep your chest on the bench: if you have to lift it to raise the dumbbells, the weight is too heavy.
When you finish, set the dumbbells on the floor before getting up.
matices: A study on the latissimus dorsi found that the chest-supported row, held isometrically, was the contraction that best served to measure the muscle’s maximal activation. We have found no study comparing it with other rows in motion; the usual reason for using it is that the bench supports the torso and the lower back does not have to hold the lean.

fuentes.titulo: Electromyographic assessment of isometric and dynamic activation characteristics of the latissimus dorsi muscle
